$comment: Authoritative attestation reference for the production publicai-gateway CVM. Fetched at runtime by the /proof page. composeHash was read back from the CVM's RTMR3 event log on 2026-09-18 and cross-checked against the Phala control-plane API; both report 25ac7eec. The sub2api image digest is the linux/amd64 child of the cosign-signed proof-v40 index (INDEX f4e7244c) built by publish-tee-images run 35203000886 from commit 91ad56b01; the attestor image is deliberately left at its proof-v20 pin because deploy/attestor carries no change since that release. HOW THE IMAGE DIGEST WAS RESOLVED, stated plainly because proof-v38 got this wrong and took production down for about 15 minutes: the amd64 child was resolved with deploy/phala/pin-amd64.sh, which parses `imagetools inspect --raw` as JSON and matches on the platform field; the compose pin was then re-checked with the same script's --verify mode; the index children were listed and read by a human (4078c938 linux/amd64 vs c545414e unknown/unknown attestation-manifest); and finally the pinned digest was actually docker-pulled and inspected - linux/amd64, entrypoint present, 140 MB - which an attestation-manifest cannot satisfy. VERIFICATION SCOPE: composeHash, the image digests and the build commit were each read back from a live source, and composeHash was cross-checked against two independent ones (RTMR3 event log and control plane). The cosign keyless signature was NOT verified locally for this release - cosign is not installed on the release machine - though the signing workflow run succeeded and anyone can verify certificate identity https://github.com/FiiLabs/sub2api/.github/workflows/publish-tee-images.yml@refs/heads/feat/two-sided-market plus the embedded githubWorkflowSha against the sourceCommit below. This release adds one operator-facing feature and touches no schema: a configurable homepage campaign banner. Homepage copy is otherwise compiled into the frontend i18n chunks, so changing a single word required rebuilding the image, redeploying the CVM, reading composeHash back and publishing a new attestation reference - a disproportionate cost for announcing a campaign, and campaigns recur. The banner is driven by a new homepage_banner_settings key serving a public unauthenticated GET /api/v1/home/banner, carries Chinese and English copy plus per-language CTA links, and ships OFF by default: with no configuration the homepage renders exactly as before. Write-path validation rejects structural mistakes outright (enabled with no text, a button label without a link, a non-http(s) URL, an unknown variant) while clamping overlong text, and the read path fails closed so a corrupt value hides the banner rather than rendering a broken one at the most prominent position on the site. There is NO schema migration in this release - the banner lives in a single JSON settings key. Verified before rollout: full backend build and vet, the entire backend unit suite (58 packages) including the banner settings tests, frontend type-check, and the full vitest suite (2081 passing). Two defects that only a real browser could surface were found and fixed during local verification: the banner shared the header's z-index and swallowed clicks aimed at the language menu, and the dismissal memory was keyed on rendered copy so switching language made a dismissed banner flicker back and forth - the key is now a language-independent content fingerprint served by the backend. A full postgres backup was taken and verified immediately beforehand - downloaded from S3, gzip-tested, 110 COPY sections - kept as a rollback point even though no schema changed. Earlier in this line: proof-v39 (per-campaign online-day buckets, new-contributor-only rewards, idle account re-check), proof-v38 (supply incentive rules engine), proof-v37 (supply/demand gate, homepage stats), proof-v36 (OpenAI contributor sharing, migration 239), proof-v35 (upstream sync to 0.2.1 plus GPT-6 Astra), v34, v33, v32, v31, v29, v28, v27, v26, v24..v15. osImageHash, appId and instanceId are unchanged; the deploy passed --no-dev-os explicitly, because phala deploy silently switches to a dev OS image when it detects a local SSH key and a dev OS would void the attestation, and the control plane confirms is_dev false after the rollout. This rollout completed in 81 seconds with no incident.
